chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man in ihram who broke an ostrich egg, and in the egg were chicks that had moved. He said: Upon him is, for every chick that moved, a camel which he slaughters in the place of slaughter.

key_terms.بَعِيرٌ: A camel (used here as the unit of compensation)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration) for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for breaking an ostrich egg while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s al-Ishtibār details the specific fidya for breaking an ostrich egg with live embryos, establishing a one-camel penalty per moving chick. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of linking compensation to the degree of life development, distinguishing it from other animal sacrifices in the Quranic tradition of Hajj penalties.
